problem_text:
A maritime logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over a voyage schedule spanning 20 consecutive port calls.  
The initial stock available at the departure of the first leg is 13 kiloliters.  
At each port call \( t = 1, \dots, 20 \), the supplier permits the company to requisition a shipment whose volume must fall between 0 and 47 kiloliters.  
However, every shipment requested will require a lead time of 2 port calls before it becomes available for consumption or for replenishing the onboard reserve.  

The projected consumption of the additive at each port call is specified as follows:  
* Leg 1: 55 kiloliters  
* Leg 2: 26 kiloliters  
* Leg 3: 22 kiloliters  
* Leg 4: 41 kiloliters  
* Leg 5: 40 kiloliters  
* Leg 6: 26 kiloliters  
* Leg 7: 42 kiloliters  
* Leg 8: 35 kiloliters  
* Leg 9: 18 kiloliters  
* Leg 10: 48 kiloliters  
* Leg 11: 41 kiloliters  
* Leg 12: 27 kiloliters  
* Leg 13: 21 kiloliters  
* Leg 14: 54 kiloliters  
* Leg 15: 10 kiloliters  
* Leg 16: 23 kiloliters  
* Leg 17: 31 kiloliters  
* Leg 18: 26 kiloliters  
* Leg 19: 55 kiloliters  
* Leg 20: 55 kiloliters  

Shortfalls are permissible, but any unsatisfied consumption will not be deferred to later legs.  
Throughout the voyage schedule, additive quantities may be treated as continuous, and the total volume held onboard at any moment must not exceed the tank capacity of 37 kiloliters.  

The aggregate expense over the entire schedule comprises three elements: the procurement cost, amounting to 3 currency units per kiloliter ordered; the storage cost, amounting to 3 currency units per kiloliter retained from one leg to the next; and the deficiency penalty, amounting to 9 currency units per kiloliter of unmet consumption. Determine the optimal shipment volume for each port call and monitor the consequent stock and deficit levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
